dcterms:description.@value: "A Tale About Lies and How Swiftly They Spread Across the Earth"

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 2: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 2: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:description.@value: "Suppose you sold me a young mare and suppose I brought it from you."
"If it is done honestly and in God's way, then, I suppose, commerce is a godly business."

o:title: A Tale About Lies,  page 4: The Church of Nicholas the Sinner

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies,  page 4: The Church of Nicholas the Sinner

dcterms:description.@value: "Let the mare remain here, while I fetch my money."
"Ermil was sitting on a plank above them, dangling beneath the roof as he whitewashed the walls of the church Nicholas the Sinner."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 6: Ermil and the mare

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 6: Ermil and the mare

dcterms:description.@value: "The mare jerked and, out of fear, bolted, and carried Ermil out of the yard and into the village street."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 7: Ermil, the mare, and Baba

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 7: Ermil, the mare, and Baba

dcterms:description.@value: "For the mare happened by Ermil's own hut just as his Baba emerged from the gate."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 8: Baba, Ermil, and the mare

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 8: Baba, Ermil, and the mare

dcterms:description.@value: "Ermil, unfortunately, hit his head on the roof of the shed and fell off the mare and lay in the yard motionless."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 9: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 9: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:description.@value: "But because of the blow he had suffered, something in Ermil's head had changed and there he lay, eyes blinking, looking at his wife and not saying a word."
"On the one hand, she pitied Ermil, but on the other, she was desperate to find out what had happened."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 11: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 11: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:description.@value: "Three times in the night she turned and whispered to her husband with the same questions, but Ermil's answer was always the same: 'I don't have any idea, I don't have a clue.'"

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 12: Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 12: Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "The red-haired Titus returned with his money."
"I command you, Titus, go pick up the mare."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 14: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 14: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:description.@value: "They went to investigate -- but there was no mare."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 15: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 15: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "'You took my mare,' Father Meager yelled. 'And now you demand your money back?!'"
"The sky turned pitch dark, but they remained by the church arguing."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 17: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 17: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "We will ask that man who was whitewashing the church where the mare went... he was here, perhaps he saw something... let him tell us!"
"But Ermil's Baba thought out a plan."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 19: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 19: Ermil and Baba

dcterms:description.@value: "Baba positioned herself behind Ermil, aimed well and hit him square on the back of his head -- on the very same spot Ermil had bumped on the roof of the shed."
"Ermil was surprised. 'What mare are you talking about?'"
"'I know nothing about that!' replied his wife. 'The mare stands tied in my shed -- how can anyone sell it but me?'"

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 22: Ermil, Baba, and the mare

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 22: Ermil, Baba, and the mare

dcterms:description.@value: "They had not walked more than a few steps when she aimed well and hit Ermil square on the back of his head."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 23: Ermil

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 23: Ermil

dcterms:description.@value: "'I don't have any idea. I don't have a clue.'"
"Ermil arrived at the church where the priest and the red-haired Titus were waiting for him."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 25: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 25: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:description.@value: "Ermil's Baba instituted her own custom: hitting her husband on the back of his head every morning before he left for work and again when he returned in the evening."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 26: Father Meager

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 26: Father Meager

dcterms:description.@value: "Only Ermil's wife enjoyed life, as she waited for the foal to arrive."
"The little fire inside was gleaming as Titus peered in and saw Ermil's Baba performing her custom over her husband's head."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 28: Baba, Ermil, and Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 28: Baba, Ermil, and Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "'What kind of mare is he talking about?' thought Titus.

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 29: Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 29: Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "And so Titus returned to his hut and sat down and started thinking."
"He walked under Ermil's windows and peered in, examining everything down to the smallest detail."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 31: Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 31: Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "No sooner had Ermil returned from work and sat down to eat his supper than his wife -- according to instituted custom -- smacked Ermil back into his smart mode and Titus walked in the door."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 32: Baba

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 32: Baba

dcterms:description.@value: "When Baba saw the red-haired Titus and heard Ermil's words, she began to tremble all over."
"But Baba's fears were in vain. The red-haired Titus did not let Ermil speak."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 34: Ermil and Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 34: Ermil and Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "As the red-haired Titus spoke this way, he was nearly in tears, and kept moving closer and closer to Ermil."
"The red-haired Titus began to kiss and to hug Ermil in all kinds of ways."
"Baba was astonished that the visit had gone so well."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 37: The mare

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 37: The mare

dcterms:description.@value: "In the morning, she woke cheerful, humming to herself."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 38: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 38: Titus and Father Meager

dcterms:description.@value: "Baba had no idea what kind of trouble awaited her because of Titus' visit."
"The red-haired Titus had enough and refused to speak with Baba any longer -- he walked straight into the shed and the others followed."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 40: Titus, Father Meager, Ermil, Baba, and the mare

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 40: Titus, Father Meager, Ermil, Baba, and the mare

dcterms:description.@value: "She grabbed onto the mare's tail and refused to let go."

o:title: A Tale About Lies, page 41: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:title.@value: A Tale About Lies, page 41: Father Meager and Titus

dcterms:description.@value: "They led the mare through the street, with Baba rocking on the tail."
"'Wait a minute,' said the priest. 'I sold you the mare without a foal -- that was one price.'"
"Ermil finished whitewashing the church of Nicholas the Sinner; the mare had long since brought forth a foal; but they continued to argue."
"The mare, in the meantime, brought forth yet another foal."
"They spent everything they had, till the last kopeck -- until there was nothing left to keep the horses."
"So, they started accepting donations. Whoever made a donation was permitted to join the argument."
"The herd grows bigger, and so does the crowd."
"One would assume that, for as long as there is space on this earth, the end is not in sight."
